paite: Huan Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
english: Then Job answered,

paite: Chihtaktakin huchi ahi chih ka thei hi: himahleh Pathian lakah mihing bangchiin a dik thei dia?
english: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

paite: Amah kisel pih a utlam a hihleh, sang khata khat amah a dawng theikei ding hi.
english: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

paite: Amah lungtangin a pila, hatnain a thilhihthei ahi: amah douin kua a kikhauhsakin, a lohchingta a oi?
english: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?

paite: Mualte a suana, a theikei ua, heha amaute a lumleh laiin.
english: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

paite: A mun akipanin lei a singa, huan huaia khuamte aling uh.
english: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

paite: Ni thu a piaa, huan a suak kei; aksite a bilhkhum ngiungeu hi.
english: He commands the sun, and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.

paite: Amah kian vante a phalhkhiaa, tuipi kihawt tungah a pai hi.
english: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

paite: Aman Jangkhua, Zuheisuktun leh Siguk leh simlam aksi tamna munte a bawl hi.
english: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

paite: Aman sui theih vuallouh thil thupite a hiha; ahi, sim zohlouh thillamdangte.
english: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

paite: Ngaiin, ka kiangah a paia, amah ka mu kei: a pai lailaia, himahleh amah ka mu kei hi.
english: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

paite: Ngaiin, samat a mana, amah kuan a kham thei dia? Bang hih na hia? kuan a kiangah a chi dia.
english: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

paite: Pathianin a hehna a lakik kei ding; Rahab panpihmite amah nuaiah a kun petmah uhi.
english: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

paite: Bangchipheta tawm jawin amah ka dawngin, amah toh ngaihtuah dingin ka thute ka telkhe dia?
english: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?

paite: Amah, diktatta zongleng, ka dawng kei ding hi; ka gal kiangah thilngetna ka bawl ding.
english: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

paite: Samta leng la, huan honna dawngta leh; himahleh ka aw a ngaikhia chih ka um kei ding hi.
english: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

paite: Huihpiin aman a honkitamsaka, a san omlouin ka liamnate a pungsak hi.
english: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

paite: Ka nak a honphal keia, himahleh thangpaihnain a hondimsak hi.
english: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

paite: Hatna thu gen leng, ngaiin, Amah a hat hi: huan vaihawmna thu, kuan hun a pe dia?
english: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

paite: Diktatta zongleng, ka kamin a honmohpaih hi: hoihkim ta zongleng, hoihlouin a hontelsak ding hi.
english: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.

paite: Hoih kim mahleng, ka kilimsak kei; ka hinna ka musit.
english: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.

paite: Khat ahi veka; huaijiakin, Hoihkim leh gilou a hihse tuak, ka chi
english: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

paite: Jepnain thakhatin hihlum leh, mi hoih thuakna a nuihsan ding hi.
english: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

paite: Lei mi gilou khuta piakin a om: huaia vaihawmmite maitangte a tuama; amah ahihkeileh, kua a hita dia?
english: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

paite: Tuin ka nite laitaipihmi sangin a kinjaw: a tai mang ua, hoih a mu kei uh.
english: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away, they see no good,

paite: Long kinte bangin a pai mang uhi: muvanlai samat tunga ngumkiak bangin.
english: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

paite: Ka phunna ka mang ngilh dia, ka mel lungkham ka pai dia, ka kipak ding, chi leng.
english: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’

paite: Ka lungkhamna tengteng ka laua, hoih non sa kei ding chih ka thei hi.
english: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.

paite: Mohpaihin ka om dia; ahihleh bangdia a thawna semgim ka hia?
english: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

paite: Vuk tuiin kisilin, ka khutte huchitakin siangsak ngeitak leng;
english: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

paite: Hinapiin guam sungah na honpai lut thou dia, huan keimah puanten a hon kih ding uh.
english: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes shall abhor me.

paite: Kei bangin, amah lah mihing ahi keia, amah ka dawn theihna dingin, vaihawmnaa ka hoh khawm theihna ding un.
english: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

paite: Ka kikal uah kou gel honmat theihna dingin, thulaigenmi a om kei hi.
english: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

paite: Kei akipanin achiang la meng henla a kihtakhuainain kei honlausak kei hen:Huaichiangin thu ka gen dia, amah ka lau kei ding: keimah ah lah huchibang ka hi ngal kei a.
english: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

paite: Huaichiangin thu ka gen dia, amah ka lau kei ding: keimah ah lah huchibang ka hi ngal kei a.
english: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
